definitions.gloss: to start over; to reset; to make a fresh start
definitions.explanation: To go back to the beginning and try again from scratch, especially after a failed attempt or stalled situation. Originally a sumo term for resetting a bout when wrestlers fail to charge properly.

examples.japanese: ⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}そう。
⟦{交渉|こうしょう}→交渉：02727_koushou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦うまく→うまい：01279_umai⟧いかなかった⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}すことにした。
examples.english: The negotiations didn't go well, so we decided to start fresh.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一度|いちど}→一度：01312_ichido⟧{気持|きも}ち⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦リセット→リセット：11199_risetto⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦ゼロ→ゼロ：01011_zero⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}した⟦ほうがいい→ほうがいい：10078_hougaii⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: I think it's better to reset your mindset and start over from zero.

notes:
Originally from sumo wrestling, where ⟦{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}し→仕切り直し：16259_shikirinaoshi⟧ refers to the wrestlers returning to their starting positions to retry the initial charge ({立|た}ち{合|あ}い) when they fail to synchronize. The word has been widely adopted in everyday and business Japanese to mean starting over.

USAGE:
Often used when a project, negotiation, or plan has stalled or failed and needs to be restarted from the beginning. Carries a positive, proactive nuance — the speaker is choosing to try again rather than giving up.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}す — to restart a plan
- ⟦{交渉|こうしょう}→交渉：02727_koushou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}す — to restart negotiations
- ⟦{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}し→仕切り直し：16259_shikirinaoshi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ — to become a do-over
- ⟦ゼロ→ゼロ：01011_zero⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{仕切|しき}り{直|なお}す — to start over from zero

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦やり{直|なお}す→やり直す：03172_yarinaosu⟧ — to redo; more general, applies to any task or action
- ⟦{出直|でなお}す→出直す：06346_denaosu⟧ — to start fresh; implies going away and coming back to try again
- ⟦{白紙|はくし}に{戻|もど}す→白紙に戻す：19685_hakushinimodosu⟧ — to return to a blank slate; emphasizes canceling everything decided so far
